summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability) needed discussion before planning, reconcile stale/pending todos across Phases 70-73, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 end-to-end (followed by CI firefighting when web-e2e/desktop-e2e broke).
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and rescoped 72/73; diagnosed and fixed three CI regressions across PRs #600 and #601 (both merged); planned and executed all 10 Phase 72 plans (SC#1-#6 covered); fixed 113 pre-existing test-file TypeScript errors and wired a build-first, test-inclusive typecheck into CI; Phase 72 verification/ship was in progress (resolving stale skipped tests) when the transcript ends.

repo: CipherBox closes todos by deleting the file from pending/ (mirrored into completed/) rather than any status flag — a phase that ships without this step leaves stale-but-done todos sitting in pending/.

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PR authors must manually dispatch against their branch (`gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>`, not `-f ref=`) to get real e2e signal before merging.

Playwright web-e2e's `ciFloor()` helper only raises wait timeouts to 60s under `process.env.CI` — locally waits stay at their bare value (often 15-30s), so local runs are systematically tighter than what CI actually enforces and can flake on tests that pass reliably in CI.

`webServer.reuseExistingServer` in playwright.config.ts is `!process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally (to get the 60s ciFloor) fights an already-running local stack unless reuse is temporarily patched to always-true.

Root `pnpm typecheck` only ran each package's `build` (tsconfig.build.json, which excludes tests) plus tsconfig.scripts.json — test files were never typechecked in CI even though each package's base tsconfig.json includes them.

`@cipherbox/*` packages resolve via workspace symlinks to each package's built `dist` (no path aliases or TS project references) — a package's typecheck requires its upstream deps already built, so typecheck must run build-first/interleaved, not before all builds.

vitest v3.2.4 changed `Mock` generic typing from v2's `Mock<[Args]>` form, and Phase 62's type retirement (FileMetadata/FolderChild/FolderEntry/FolderMetadata/rootFolderKey) left widespread drift in test fixtures across packages/sdk.
1Password SSH commit signing can hang/timeout the `git commit` shell call even though the commit actually lands — always verify via `git log`/`git status` rather than trusting a timeout as failure.
GitHub Actions cargo/fuse checks fail on macOS for Windows-only deps (`windows-future`) — known, unrelated to code changes; Windows CI is authoritative for that leg.

`gh workflow run` with `-f ref=<branch>` can 422 with 'Unexpected inputs' if main's workflow definition predates that input name — use `--ref <branch>` instead, which runs the workflow from that branch's definition.

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty'; a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-triggering it collided with Phase 71's new anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS before first-publish and routing 'Found' into the existing CAS-retry path instead of blindly re-sealing at seq=1.

publish_with_cas_retry is the shared CAS helper for both folder-publish and file-publish callers; threading an optional preresolved_seq through it (from the resolve done by the new first-publish guard) avoids a redundant second IPNS resolve on the Found path, per Greptile's P2 suggestion.

refreshSharedFolder write-envelope staleness (68.2 backlog item 4) overlaps Phase 73's write03-refresh-access scope but lives in a bundled 10-item cross-area backlog todo — not cleanly foldable whole into either phase.

Test helper read stale IndexedDB store names (generation-high-water/seq-high-water) after Phase 70.1 collapsed them into a single rotation-floor store (DB v2, keyed by nodeId) — helper bailed early and returned undefined, masking as a durability bug when the product path was actually intact.

Test driver used pre-Phase-71 share DTO field names (readDescriptorRef, rootIpnsName) in the /shares POST body and share reads, tripping the API's forbidNonWhitelisted ValidationPipe with a 400 after the underlying FUSE bug was fixed.

Test 21 (D-06) asserted exactly one-200-plus-one-409 for concurrent first-publish, but Phase 71's same-CID idempotency legitimately allows two 200s; rewritten to accept both outcomes while still rejecting any 5xx or a loser that isn't 409.

workflow: When a subagent reports a completed CI/test run, verify with a direct log/status pull before acting — do not trust a summary alone (e.g., the sdk-e2e failure on #600 looked caused-by-the-PR but was an unrelated pre-existing flake).

For unattended long-running phase execution, prefer sequential execution on the main tree over parallel worktrees when the plans are heavily serialized on one file (client.ts) and the repo is a pnpm monorepo (worktrees lack node_modules by default).

When new out-of-scope tech debt surfaces mid-execution (e.g., pre-existing test-file TS errors discovered while running plan 72-04), capture it as a durable todo file immediately and sequence the fix as an explicit final plan rather than silently deferring or scope-creeping the current plan.
After a scope-checking AskUserQuestion returns 'clarify' rather than a decision, proactively re-derive the answer by reading the source material directly rather than re-asking a vague question.
Use TaskCreate to track multi-hour, multi-plan executions across context so directives (like 'fix all TS drift, wire CI') survive and don't get dropped mid-run.

When local test-timeout flakiness repeatedly blocks verification of a fix, switch to running under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (CI=1) rather than repeatedly bumping individual local timeouts ad hoc — but be ready for config side effects (e.g., webServer reuse) that require a temporary, reverted patch.

friction: Initially checked the wrong todo directory (resolved/ instead of completed/), requiring user correction.
`gh workflow run -f ref=` was rejected with HTTP 422 before discovering `--ref <branch>` was the correct dispatch form.

Local web-e2e verification became a multi-round whack-a-mole: five separate local runs were each blocked by a different flaky test (4.10, 4.11, 2.1) due to CI/local timeout asymmetry (ciFloor), before switching to a CI-equivalent local run to get a clean signal.
Setting CI=1 locally to match CI's timeout floor broke `reuseExistingServer`, requiring a temporary playwright.config.ts patch (backed up and reverted afterward).
A buggy `cat-file` check caused temporary confusion about whether the 8 todo-move commits had actually landed, requiring a second decisive check of HEAD tree contents.
The GSD hooks JSON contains raw/multiline string values that broke normal JSON parsing twice, requiring custom lenient-parser scripts to extract research/tdd/schema-gate fragments.
`git commit` hung/timed out repeatedly due to a 1Password SSH signing prompt, producing false-negative failures that had to be re-verified via git log each time.

Discovered mid-execution that CI never typechecked test files at all, and that fixing this properly required migrating ~113 errors across 15 files off retired Phase-62 types rather than a quick mechanical patch — a much larger unplanned side effort.
sdk-e2e failure on PR #600 initially looked caused by the PR's diff but was an unrelated pre-existing Test 21 flake, requiring a diagnostic agent to rule out causation.
#601's desktop-e2e initially failed on Windows/Linux after the FUSE fix landed, turning out to be a separate stale `.mts` test-driver DTO field-name issue layered on top of the real fix.
